en: Mayon Volcano's steep slopes make deadly lahars travel very fast during heavy rains, so residents must evacuate immediately.
After a strong earthquake near the Davao Oriental coast, immediately move to higher ground to avoid a deadly tsunami.
The Sierra Madre mountain range on Luzon acts as a natural barrier that slows down typhoons coming from the Pacific Ocean.
The Pasig River in Metro Manila is heavily polluted, so you should never swim in it or drink its untreated water.
Tuguegarao in Cagayan often records the highest temperatures in the Philippines, so residents must drink plenty of water to avoid heatstroke.
Stagnant water in flooded areas of Metro Manila breeds Aedes mosquitoes that carry the deadly dengue virus.
Mount Pulag in Benguet has freezing temperatures at its peak, so hikers must wear thick jackets to prevent hypothermia.
Visitors exploring the Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan must wear helmets to protect their heads from low cave ceilings.
Touching the vibrant corals in the Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park can cause painful skin cuts and destroy the fragile marine habitat.
When Taal Volcano in Batangas erupts, wearing an N95 mask protects your lungs from inhaling harmful, abrasive volcanic ash.
Lake Lanao in Mindanao is very deep, so children must always wear life jackets when riding a boat to prevent drowning.
Deforestation in the mountainous provinces of Ifugao increases the risk of deadly landslides during the heavy rains of the monsoon season.
